svg.text: The internet works by IP address, but names like google.com cannot be

text.font-family: ui-monospace, 'Cascadia Mono', 'Segoe UI Mono', Consolas, 'DejaVu Sans Mono', monospace

svg.text: turned into addresses. That is why pages will not open even though you

svg.text: - DNS server address wrong, stale, or belonging to an old network

svg.text: - Configured DNS server not responding (router DNS proxy or VPN DNS

svg.text: 1. Clear the DNS cache first (safe, instant)

text.font-family: ui-monospace, 'Cascadia Mono', 'Segoe UI Mono', Consolas, 'DejaVu Sans Mono', monospace

svg.text: 2. If it continues, switch this computer to a reliable public DNS

text.font-family: ui-monospace, 'Cascadia Mono', 'Segoe UI Mono', Consolas, 'DejaVu Sans Mono', monospace
ui-monospace, 'Cascadia Mono', 'Segoe UI Mono', Consolas, 'DejaVu Sans Mono', monospace

svg.text: 3. If a VPN is connected, disconnect it and retest

text.font-family: ui-monospace, 'Cascadia Mono', 'Segoe UI Mono', Consolas, 'DejaVu Sans Mono', monospace

svg.text: 4. Re-test name resolution - GeeNet will verify the fix

text.font-family: ui-monospace, 'Cascadia Mono', 'Segoe UI Mono', Consolas, 'DejaVu Sans Mono', monospace
